https://www.barrons.com/articles/betting-on-a-smoother-ride-for-tech-stocks-1533330236 Betting on a Smoother Ride for Tech Stocks By Updated Aug. 3, 2018 5:27 p.m. ET Text Size Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg Illustration: BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP/Getty Images By Gunjan Banerji Updated Aug. 3, 2018 5:27 p.m. ET
Shares of technology companies have swung wildly—but options investors don’t need to take a bullish or bearish stance to profit from their recent volatility.
Investors ambivalent about the future direction of stocks like Facebook (ticker: FB) but looking to take advantage of the high turbulence in tech shares could tap a trade called a “strangle” on the social-media giant, says Tom Sosnoff, founder of tastytrade, an options-focused media company.
This would entail simultaneously selling both a call option and a put option expiring in September at $190 and $155, respectively. Calls confer the right to buy shares; puts give the right to sell shares.
The high expected swings in the stock and its liquidity—or ease of trading—make it a good time to sell the options, Sosnoff says. Investors have flocked to Facebook options lately, and when expected swings are higher, options prices rise. The shares have also recorded big swings, Trade Alert data show. An investor, he says, would earn $300 from selling the two contracts, which wager that the stock will stay relatively rangebound—that is, won’t fall below $155 or higher than $190 over the next seven weeks. Newsletter Sign-up
Because expected swings in tech shares are high, it’s a profitable time to put on the trade. Facebook, which was crushed after its earnings report on July 25 , closed at $176.37 on Thursday, down about 8% since the beginning of June.
After Facebook’s earnings revealed a tempered outlook on advertising growth, tech has been on edge. It was one of the worst-performing sectors in the week before it led the stock market down on Monday.
The NYSE FANG+ Index, which tracks Facebook, Amazon.com (AMZN), Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL), Apple (AAPL), Twitter (TWTR), Tesla (TSLA), Nvidia (NVDA), Alibaba Group Holding (BABA), and Baidu (BIDU), entered correction territory this past week.
It isn’t the first time tech moves have triggered broader market gyrations. Earlier this year, concerns about regulatory risks surrounding Facebook and its data-use standards sent stocks into a tailspin.
Options traders, too, have been jittery about tech, sending a measure dubbed skew—which measures how expensive it is to hedge stock declines—to a record high recently. Meanwhile, traders are forecasting greater swings in the tech-heavy PowerShares QQQ Trust exchange-traded fund (QQQ), even though most tech heavyweights have already revealed earnings. The ETF’s implied volatility rose four percentage points to 17% the week before last, according to Credit Suisse.
“The question going forward is whether this will be viewed as an idiosyncratic miss or if we will see further de-risking in the sector,” wrote Credit Suisse equity derivatives strategist Mandy Xu in a July 30 note. More on Tech
